quotes.quote: **Referential anchoring test.** The label is decided by whether the phrase refers to a concrete, identifiable disorder, not by its surface form.

A condition-suffixed head noun, a plural count inflection, or a type-modifier-plus-head structure does not by itself make a phrase a Disease Class, and the label applies even when the phrase has no eponym, acronym, or proper name. The full mention span is treated as one unit, so a type modifier does not turn it into a subtype class (see "classical galactosemia," Example 15).
Use the smallest span necessary to include all tokens expressing the most specific form of the disease.
